findings.reason: Confirmed, with an essential correction to the proposed duality statement. K-book IV.6.9 (p.59), the building/Steinberg discussion in Church–Farb–Putman §1.4, and R.1/N.3:finite-generation expose the missing rank-filtration and Steinberg-coefficient finiteness inputs; ALS.2's compactification alone is not that package. But the untwisted Steinberg module is NOT always the GL_n(O) dualizing module. Putman–Studenmund, arXiv:1909.01217v4, Theorem C (p.4), gives D = St_n(F) tensor (Z_chi)^(tensor(n−1)), chi = Norm(F/Q) composed with determinant. Use this twist, or first pass to a torsion-free finite-index subgroup in ker chi and prove descent. Their p.2 permits integral coefficients for torsion-free groups; rational duality alone does not prove integral finite generation. Put building, Solomon–Tits and the correctly twisted arithmetic duality/finiteness interface in R.1, importing ALS.2/its early finite-level cohomology. N.3 owns the Q-rank filtration and the assembly for Aut(P), including nonfree projectives, low ranks and the finite-S localization step. Do not duplicate the arithmetic finiteness proof there. Pinned searches found no supplier of this building/duality package; the named Steinberg files concern different objects.

Confirmed. M.5's field diagonal norm-residue isomorphism does not itself state the truncated motivic-complex comparison consumed by M.6/M.7. K-book VI.4.1–4.2 (p.16) distinguishes the Beilinson–Lichtenbaum comparison from the diagonal symbol theorem and then uses it for the spectral sequence. PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21/166 explicitly routes the truncated comparison to M.5/M.7 without supplying its missing node. Add a source-level Beilinson–Lichtenbaum node after the norm-residue engine: specify the morphism from the motivic complex modulo an invertible prime power to the truncated derived pushforward of the étale Tate twist, its topology, naturality and degree conventions, and prove the passage from fields to the smooth schemes actually used. Treat the Dedekind-base arithmetic version and localization separately. M.7 imports this comparison before deriving Quillen–Lichtenbaum; it must not infer it merely from the diagonal equality.

Confirmed. K-book VI.3.1 (p.12) supplies Suslin's finite-coefficient comparison with BO for the real field, and VI.9.1–9.4 (pp.50–52) uses real-place information in the dyadic calculation. The existing RT.4:topological contract supplies complex topological K-theory, not a real KO/BO package; Tau Ceti's Clifford-algebra Bott periodicity is not topological Bott periodicity. Extend that shared topological owner with real K-theory, its periodicity and complexification/realification comparisons, then give the algebraic-to-real comparison a theorem node feeding M.7. State the comparison's degree and coefficient hypotheses (the cited positive-degree theorem starts at n ≥ 1; degree zero needs its own identification), and preserve the real-place maps and extensions used by N.5. No second dyadic calculation belongs in N.5.

Confirmed. The integrated K.4 additivity/relative-S nodes and H.5:S-delooping node explicitly say that the latter proof uses K-book V.1.7 (p.8), which in turn uses additivity. The stage ordering places the full K.4 after this delooping although the packet supplies a reverse node link. Move the additivity theorem and the relative-S fibration/delooping proof into the early K.4:construction prefix; H.5:S-delooping then assembles the iterated connective spectrum from that proof, and later K.4 retains fibration, approximation and comparison results needing it. Move K-theory-specific biexact products/coherence to K.7; keep generic smash-product infrastructure in H.5:spectra. Update both packet parents/links and stage dependencies together. A pending restructuring proposal is not an applied repair.

Confirmed with scope restrictions. K-book IV Ex.1.3 and §4 (pp.14,38–45), Hatcher Prop.4.72–4.74 (printed pp.416–418), and the H.3/H.4 proof steps require obstruction theory and homological Whitehead for simple or connected H-spaces. Upstream AlgebraicTopology Stage 8 only promises the simply connected homological version; the pinned HSpace structure is not itself a theorem of simplicity or homotopy associativity. Put the required simple-space/CW-type theorem, the H-space simplicity bridge and the scoped extension/uniqueness obstruction argument in H.3, with explicit fundamental-group action hypotheses. Add H.3 → H.4 for its plus comparison. Coordinate the rational Hurewicz requirement with finding 33: one Cartan–Serre owner in H.6, not two unrelated versions. A homology isomorphism of arbitrary spaces, or an arbitrary fibration over a simply connected base, is not enough.

Confirmed, narrowing the negative search and the requested theorem. Borel 1977 §§2.2–2.4 (printed pp.617–619; formulas checked visually) constructs an inner form SL_1(D), uses compactness/strong approximation and its Tamagawa volume to obtain the zeta-factor volume formula needed by R.5. R.1/AA.2's general measure construction and Borel 1974's stable-cohomology theorem do not supply this arithmetic volume computation. Add the split-at-infinity division-algebra existence and the normalized SL_1(D) strong-approximation/Tamagawa input, importing AA.3's quotient/reduction machinery and the established Brauer/class-field interfaces rather than rebuilding them. Prove the local Euler-factor calculation and the measure comparison; tau=1 is a sufficient sourced theorem, with rational nonzero proportionality the actual regulator requirement. Do not claim every pinned strong-approximation result concerns function fields: Tau Ceti also has surjectivity of SL_2(Z) reduction modulo d. Neither that special case nor the atlas's PGL_2/Q Tamagawa computation supplies arbitrary SL_1(D). AA.2 excludes computing every Tamagawa number, not all particular computations.

Confirmed as an ownership/order defect. Keep R.3's arithmetic-order stable-cohomology/rank theorem, and let N.3:ranks derive the finite-S extension using N.2 and L.1 (with the degree-one S-unit exception). Confirmed, with a field-scope obligation in the fix. Totaro, Milnor K-theory is the simplest part of algebraic K-theory, printed pp.183–184, constructs the inverse diagonal cycle map using norms and kills boundaries by Suslin reciprocity. Do not silently identify normalization with smoothness over an imperfect field: use regular proper normalizations with the required finite residue extensions and inseparable norm compatibility, or explicitly prove the reduction to a scope where smoothness holds. Degree-two Weil reciprocity alone is not the all-degree input.

Confirmed. Bloch–Kato 1986 §2, Thm.2.1 and Lemma2.3 (printed pp.113–114), uses the differential symbol and the Cartier operator; the formula on p.113 was visually checked. For mod p define the logarithmic differential subgroup as the kernel of 1−C⁻¹ into differentials modulo exact forms, and prove the symbol isomorphism. Explain the extension from smooth characteristic-p algebras to arbitrary fields, including imperfect fields; the smooth/perfect-field contract alone is insufficient. Separate the mod-p proof from the Witt/prime-power extension and from M.5a–c's invertible-prime motivic engine.

Confirmed, correcting the generality of the proposed import. The assembled graph lacks the ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 Kummer input to M.5c; the cup-product input does not replace it. Confirmed. Confirmed. Confirmed. Confirmed. Confirmed. The integrated resolution acceptance test literally says affine LINE with doubled origin and K0VB=Z. Gluing line bundles across Spec(k[t,t⁻¹]) gives Pic(X)=k[t,t⁻¹]^×/k^×=Z; rank and determinant therefore give a surjection K0VB(X) → Z², contradicting K0VB=Z. K-book V.3.4.2 (p.22) has the same error, but II.8.2.4 (p.77) requires dimension ≥2 and II Ex.9.10(d) (p.100) explicitly uses the affine PLANE. Replace the example by that plane, retain the original resolution theorem's hypotheses, and record the source discrepancy under sourceIssues as required by §18. The author's errata URL also returned 404 in this verification; this is a proved discrepancy between the downloaded chapter versions, not a claim about every published edition.
